record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: For F in {R, C} and k ≥ 1, let C(k; F) be the set of k by k correlation matrices over F, let C1(k; F) be the subset of rank-one correlation matrices, and let acx denote absolute convex hull. Determine whether the trace-inequality form of Grothendieck’s inequality remains valid when the special block matrix J(A) = (1/2)[[0, A], [A*, 0]] is replaced by an arbitrary matrix B in M(k × k; F); equivalently, determine whether C(k; F) is contained in K_G^F acx(C1(k; F)) for every k.

evidence.quote: Of particular relevance is the set C1(k; F) of all k × k correlation matrices of rank 1 and the (Hermitian) block matrix J(A) := 1/2 ( 0 A A∗ 0 ), where m, n ∈ N and A ∈ M(m × n; F).

However, we don’t know whether we also may substitute in GT itself the block matrix J(A) through an arbitrary matrix B ∈ M(k × k; F). If this were the case an application of the bipolar theorem shows that the latter would be equivalent to the non-negligible set inclusion C(k; F) ⊆ K F G acx ( C1(k; F) ) for all k ∈ N, where C(k; F) denotes the set of all k × k correlation matrices with entries in F and acx the absolute convex hull (of a set).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F} \in \{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}\}$. For $k \ge 1$, let $C(k; \mathbb{F})$ denote the set of all $k \times k$ correlation matrices with entries in $\mathbb{F}$ (i.e., positive semidefinite Hermitian matrices over $\mathbb{F}$ with all diagonal entries equal to $1$), and let $C_1(k; \mathbb{F}) \subseteq C(k; \mathbb{F})$ denote the subset consisting of those correlation matrices that have rank one. For a subset $S$ of a complex vector space, write $\mathrm{acx}(S)$ for its absolute convex hull, i.e., the set of all finite sums $\sum_i \lambda_i s_i$ with $s_i \in S$ and $\sum_i |\lambda_i| \le 1$.

Let $K_G^{\mathbb{F}}$ be the Grothendieck constant for the field $\mathbb{F}$, namely the smallest constant such that for every $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every matrix $A = (a_{ij}) \in M(m \times n; \mathbb{F})$,
$$ \sup_{\substack{x_i, y_j \in B_H}} \Big| \sum_{i,j} a_{ij} \langle x_i, y_j\rangle \Big| \;\le\; K_G^{\mathbb{F}} \sup_{\substack{|s_i|, |t_j| \le 1 \\ s_i, t_j \in \mathbb{F}}} \Big| \sum_{i,j} a_{ij} s_i \overline{t_j}\Big|, $$
where $H$ ranges over Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb{F}$ and $B_H$ is its unit ball.

A trace-form of Grothendieck's inequality is known to hold when one tests against block matrices $J(A) = \tfrac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & A \\ A^* & 0\end{pmatrix}$. Determine whether the analogous trace inequality remains valid when $J(A)$ is replaced by an arbitrary square matrix $B \in M(k \times k; \mathbb{F})$. Equivalently (via the bipolar theorem), decide whether
$$ C(k; \mathbb{F}) \;\subseteq\; K_G^{\mathbb{F}} \cdot \mathrm{acx}\bigl(C_1(k; \mathbb{F})\bigr) $$
holds for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any paper resolving the inclusion $C(k;\mathbb{F}) \subseteq K_G^{\mathbb{F}}\,\mathrm{acx}(C_1(k;\mathbb{F}))$. Recent related work (e.g., Christensen 2025 on column-bounded matrices and Grothendieck's inequalities, and the 2023 survey by Oertel) discusses this question without settling it. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Column bounded matrices and Grothendieck's inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Treats Grothendieck constants and convex sets of positive matrices but does not address the inclusion C(k;F) ⊆ K_G^F · acx(C1(k;F)).
status_evidence.claim: The most recent related work does not resolve the stated inclusion.

status_evidence.title: Some points of view on Grothendieck's inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing dual/geometric formulations of Grothendieck's inequality involving convex hulls of rank-one matrices.
status_evidence.claim: The geometric reformulation in terms of absolute convex hulls of rank-one correlation matrices is discussed but the equivalence question for arbitrary B is not resolved.
